newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium bans pig imports from most of Netherlands.
newsitem.headline: Belgium bans pig imports from most of Netherlands.

text.p: Belgium has banned imports of live pigs from almost of all of the Netherlands in line with European Union moves following outbreaks of swine fever in Germany and the Netherlands, the Agriculture Ministry said.
The ban has been in force since 1900 GMT on Wednesday, the ministry said in a statement. Only pigs from the Assen and Almelo areas in the north of the Netherlands can be imported.

The measure follows a recommendation to ban live pig exports from most Dutch districts, issued on Wednesday by the EU's Standing Veterinary Committee. It is expected to be formally imposed by the European Commission in the next few days.
The Dutch goverment said the move smacked of a panic reaction. The Netherlands produced pigs and pork products worth some 5.1 billion guilders in 1996 of which about 60 percent was exported.

Belgium's pig population was 7.4 million in 1996, 96 percent of them in Flanders in the north, making it the most densely-populated part of the EU in pig terms after neighbouring southern Netherlands, where most of the cases of swine fever were found.
Belgian pork exports were worth 60 billion Belgian francs ($1.74 billion) last year, up 18 percent from 1995. --Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6810, Fax +32 2 230 7710
